query: when does something earn a place in the main playbook instead of only living in the per-run log?
answer_snippet: promote only **confirmed** techniques into METHODOLOGY/refs. A step earns its place in the methodology after it worked on a real task

query: the output is clearly wrong but all I can see is the symptom — how far should I go before I start changing things?
expected_heading: Phase 2 — DIAGNOSE (find the cause, not just a symptom)
answer_snippet: A symptom is not a cause. ... Keep going until you can name the mechanism.

query: the bug only shows up some of the time — can I move on and start diagnosing it now?
answer_snippet: Get a reliable one-command repro. A flaky repro isn't done.
also_acceptable: METHODOLOGY.md :: Phase 1 — REPRODUCE (do this fully before changing anything)

answer_snippet: the token ERR_CONN_4021 in the debug log — the kind of exact string worth recording verbatim

query: two requests with different locales come back with the same cached response — where is the actual bug?
answer_snippet: the cache key is built from the path only and omits the locale query parameter
also_acceptable: METHODOLOGY.md :: Phase 2 — DIAGNOSE (find the cause, not just a symptom)

query: how do I actually prove a fix worked instead of just assuming it did?
expected_heading: Phase 4 — VERIFY (prove it, don't assume it)
answer_snippet: Re-run the Phase 1 repro. It must now pass. That is the primary evidence.

query: what's the standard shape I should use when adding a new reference entry?
answer_snippet: Trigger -> Chain (numbered, with exact commands) -> Notes/gotchas -> Status
